messages.subject: acoustic playbacks in R?
messages.body_plain:
Dear Seewave community

I am interested in performing animal auditory behavior experiments in R using interactive playbacks of sound files.

For example, I would playback signal 1 (s1) from channel 1 and signal 2 (s2) from channel 2, and then part way through the trial replace s1 with s2 so that both channels are playing s2. Or many other permutations of this procedure.

Is this possible at the moment?

Thanks
Alex

messages.subject: TDOA with corenv
messages.body_plain:
Howdy. So leafing around through the google groups it seems that you all are quite active. First of I'll follow form I'm quite impressed with seewave and quite dependent on it for a bioacoustic project (like others here it seems). For my part I've got a 4 channel mic system running audio into a raspberry pi running a reduced linux OS (think huge ram limits like 200mb usable), sitting in a forest recording birdsongs. Now what I want it to do is go through my dawn chorus recordings (piecemeal like due to having hardly any ram) find the bird songs that come through loud and clear on all four mics, build a list of all those that can reasonably be paired as originating from the same singer. Now this part is all done and for the most part works nicely (had to scrap using timer and do most of this with env. timer was too slow and resource heavy on my bitty computers) and do some cross correlations to build a time delay matrix from which i can multilaterate out my singer (the multilateration can be done when the time delay matrix and birdie get magiked over to the lab). See once I have that time delay matrix I don't need four mics. I can drop all my channels but one, and only pull the bits of audio that actually contain resolved target song snippets, compress those down from wav to flacc and delete off all the other audio that doesn't give me good time delays with p values i like. Now everything is working all fine and dandy except corenv... which seems to hang on even tiny bits of audio like tenth of a second bits with say 22khz sample rate. I am not sure really about why that is, the example code uses a tenth of a second in the help file, I know i am a low RAM outfit, but still I am concerned if i trim it any leaner I won't have enough points to do a good cross correlation. Here's my code all annotated up. I put in a test file which is just an hour loop of the tico dataset that is included in seewave, that is all tico2.wav is.

library (tuneR)
library (seewave)

totaltime <- 61.15

starts <- seq(from = 0, to = totaltime -2 , by=2)
stops <- seq (from =2,to=totaltime,by=2)

startsb <- seq(from = 0.001, to = totaltime -2.001 , by=2)
stopsb <- seq (from =2.001,to=totaltime,by=2)

startsc <- seq(from = 0.002, to = totaltime -2.002 , by=2)
stopsc <- seq (from =2.002,to=totaltime,by=2)

startsd <- seq(from = 0.003, to = totaltime -2.003 , by=2)
stopsd <- seq (from =2.003,to=totaltime,by=2)

MidFreq <- 3000
Temperature <- 20
Dist <- 1
cushion <- .003*60

mic1 <- readWave("tico2.wav", from = starts[1], to = stops[1], units = "minutes")
mic2 <- readWave("tico2.wav", from = startsb[1], to = stopsb[1], units = "minutes")
mic3 <- readWave("tico2.wav", from = startsc[1], to = stopsc[1], units = "minutes")
mic4 <- readWave("tico2.wav", from = startsd[1], to = stopsd[1], units = "minutes")

songtimes <- function(mic,Flatbirds,Sharpbirds,samplerate,Threshold,songcomb)
{
#Custom function
#Filter out the unused frequencies and output in useful form
mic1 <-ffilter(mic,from=Flatbirds,to=Sharpbirds, output = "matrix")
#amplitude time envelope the remaining signal into a string of amplitude values
#using a hilbert transform and a bit of smoothing
mis1 <- env(mic, f = samplerate, envt = "hil", ksmooth=kernel("daniell",100), plot = FALSE)
#kill the old signal
mic <-NULL
#make a dataframe to put the values in
flag1 <- data.frame(matrix(NA, nrow = length(mis1), ncol = 2))
#put the values in
flag1[,1] <- mis1
#and a time stamp
flag1[,2] <- seq(length(mis1))
#kill the old file
mis1 <- NULL
#get the highest amplitude
AMP <- max(flag1[,1])
#Detection Threshold
Thresh <- Threshold*AMP
#Now throw out all the values less than the threshold
flag1 <- subset (flag1,subset = X1 > Thresh)
#set things up to clear out all the ones that are from the same song
#do this by making an offset data frame
flagg1 <- data.frame(matrix(NA, nrow = length(flag1[,1])+1, ncol = 3))
#at this point the actual values aren't important anymore just the timestamps
#first row has an inserted first time value
flagg1[,1] <- c(NA,flag1[,2])
#second row has an inserted last time value
flagg1[,2] <- c(flag1[,2],NA)
#kill flag1
flag1 <- NULL
#get the difference between them
flagg1[,3] <- abs(flagg1[,2]-flagg1[,1])
songstamps <- subset (flagg1, X3 > songcomb, select = X2)
#kill flagg1
flagg1 <- NULL
#Then we need to put that into seconds
#This leaves the timestamps of all the songs
songstamps <- songstamps/samplerate

songstamps
}

#Values for computation
#Flatbirds <- 2000
#Sharpbirds <- 6000
#samplerate <- 22050
#Threshold <- .1
#songcomb <- .2*samplerate

#Use the function built for song times to get times for each mic
one <- songtimes(mic1,2000,6000,22050,.1,.2*22050)
#kill mic1
mic1 <- NULL
two <- songtimes(mic2,2000,6000,22050,.1,.2*22050)
#kill mic2
mic2 <- NULL
three <- songtimes(mic3,2000,6000,22050,.1,.2*22050)
#kill mic3
mic3 <- NULL
four <- songtimes(mic4,2000,6000,22050,.1,.2*22050)
mic4 <- NULL

#combine them into one dataframe
#by first getting the size needed
size <- max(c(length(one[,1]),length(two[,1]),length(three[,1]),length(four[,1])))
#making the dataframe
songs <- data.frame(matrix(NA, nrow = size, ncol = 4))

#fill dataframe with song times
#somewhat non-trivially since they may have unequal lengths,
#but this is the fastest way I've made
songs[1:length(one[,1]),1] <- one[,1]
songs[1:length(two[,1]),2] <- two[,1]
songs[1:length(three[,1]),3] <- three[,1]
songs[1:length(four[,1]),4] <- four[,1]
#kill song times
one <- NULL
two <- NULL
three <- NULL
four <- NULL

#Next build a dataframe of all the songs that can realistically be expected to be paired together
#Based on their arrival times
#Use the speed of sound at a middle frequency at the temperature to get a time window
Speed <- wasp(f = MidFreq, t = Temperature, c = NULL, s = NULL, d = NULL, medium = "air")
#For long mic runs a cushion may be needed for sound falloff with distance
#since the amplitude cutoff is determined as a proportion of the maximum
TimeWindow <- Dist/Speed$c + cushion

#Using one mic as a reference
#(any one will do since a resolved song needs all four)
#find all timestamps that could possibly be resultant from the same singer
#based on distance and group them together
#toss the rest

#Can't be any more confirmed songs than potential songs so make dataframe to fill that size
#Cull it after
song <- data.frame(matrix(NA, nrow = size, ncol = 4))
#Kill size
size <- NULL

for (a in 1:length(songs[,1]))
{
#get time differences for every value to the reference mics time in question
absV2 <- abs(songs[,2]-songs[a,1])
absV3 <- abs(songs[,3]-songs[a,1])
absV4 <- abs(songs[,4]-songs[a,1])
Two <- subset(songs[,2], subset = absV2 < TimeWindow)
Three <- subset(songs[,3], subset = absV2 < TimeWindow)
Four <- subset(songs[,4], subset = absV2 < TimeWindow)
if(length(Two) >= 1 & length(Three) >= 1 & length(Four) >= 1)
{
song[a,] <-c(songs[a,1],Two,Three,Four)
}
}
#at the end drop the empties
song <- song[complete.cases(song),]

#This leaves all the resolvable time stamps
#What is wanted is to do the cross correlations to build a time delay matrix
#Times for the cross correlations
Times <- apply(song,FUN = min, MARGIN =1)

Timedelays <- data.frame(matrix(NA, nrow = length(song[,1]), ncol = 3))
DelayP <- data.frame(matrix(NA, nrow = length(song[,1]), ncol = 3))
for(b in 1:length(Times))
{
#Next two are commented out since the wav file right now is just the test file
#One <- readWave("tico2.wav", from = Times[b], to = Times[b]+.001, units = "seconds")
#Two <- readWave("tico2.wav", from = Times[b], to = Times[b]+.001, units = "seconds")
#Instead I just brought back the ones from before
mic1 <- readWave("tico2.wav", from = starts[1], to = stops[1], units = "minutes")
One <- cutw(mic1, from = Times[b], to = Times[b]+.1)
mic1 <- NULL
mic2 <- readWave("tico2.wav", from = starts[1], to = stops[1], units = "minutes")
Two <- cutw(mic2, from = Times[b], to = Times[b]+.1)
mic2 <- NULL
lag <- corenv(One, Two, f= samplerate, envt="hil", msmooth = NULL, ksmooth = NULL,plot = FALSE,method = "kendall")
Two <- NULL
Timedelays[b,1] <- lag$rmax
DelayP[b,1] <- lag$p

#No sense doing them all when one doesn't work yet so they are commented out
#Three <- readWave("tico2.wav", from = Times[b], to = Times[b]+.001, units = "seconds")
#lag <- corenv(One, Three, f= samplerate, envt="hil", msmooth = NULL, ksmooth = NULL,plot = FALSE,method = "kendall")
#Three <- NULL
#Timedelays[b,2] <- lag$rmax
#DelayP[b,2] <- lag$p
#Four <- readWave("tico2.wav", from = Times[b], to = Times[b]+.001, units = "seconds")
#lag <- corenv(One, Four, f= samplerate, envt="hil", msmooth = NULL, ksmooth = NULL,plot = FALSE,method = "kendall")
#Four <- NULL
#Timedelays[b,3] <- lag$rmax
#DelayP[b,3] <- lag$p
#lag <- NULL
}

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] acoustic playbacks in R?
messages.body_plain:
Dear Alex,

I have never used R for playback experiments.

However, what you describe is probably more related to tuneR package
rather than to seewave.

See the Wave object class to manipulate left and right channels and
the function play() for playback.

You can also use several editing functions in both tuneR
(extractWave(), bind()) and seewave (cutw(), pastew(), repw() for
instance).

Sorry not to be able to help more,

Jerome

messages.subject: problem with loadSample()
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am using the function loadSample() in a loop to read the sound files. For a few of the 144 files I am working on, I get an error:

Error in dim(data) <- c(channels, length(data)/channels) :
  dims [product 428] do not match the length of object [429]

I have open the files in other sound analysis programs (Raven) without a problem.

I guess is something simple but I dont get it. Does anyone know what might be the issue?

You can download one of the files from here (https://www.dropbox.com/s/srgjze84ixbjy6c/VocatorParaguas009.WAV)

thanks in advance

Marcelo Araya-Salas
